Neuroscientist and brain coach Louisa Nicola shares an unusual method to improve brain function in this Danny Jones episode. Nicola works with athletes and executives on sleep, focus, and mental performance. Her top trick, she says, can sharpen the mind within days.

Nicola explains the science behind her method in plain talk, step by step. She covers how the brain clears waste, resets focus, and locks in learning. Jones asks how ordinary people can apply her system without a lab or a coach. Listeners who want a sharper mind get a clear routine from a working brain expert.

Matthew Cox is going Hollywood, and he tells Danny Jones how a con man made the turn to film. Cox, the former mortgage fraudster turned true-crime writer, has seen his life and stories draw screen interest. The episode follows his strange second act from fraud to film.

Cox explains which of his cases and characters Hollywood wants and why. He shares the odd feeling of watching actors play the people he scammed and served time with. Jones asks whether the glamour tempts him back toward the old life. Fascinated and amused listeners get a felon's Tinseltown chapter, told with a grin.

Forensic doctor Philippe Charlier joins Danny Jones to talk about his work on the remains of the famous dead. The episode title names Hitler, Napoleon, and Jesus. Charlier tests old bones and relics with lab tools.

Charlier tells how he tests a skull, a tooth, or a relic and reads what it can prove. He shares what his tests found in the Hitler and Napoleon cases. Jones asks what science can and cannot say about holy relics. Listeners get a calm, sharp tour of a strange job. The library keeps the talk as a record of his work and finds.

Tucker Carlson and commentator Saagar Enjeti team up on new developments in Attorney General Pam Bondi's handling of the Epstein files. Enjeti co-hosts the Breaking Points show and tracks the scandal's twists closely. Two hosts dig into one scandal that refuses to die.

The pair go through the latest releases, delays, and statements from Bondi's office. They argue the public is still being managed rather than told the truth. Carlson and Enjeti compare what was promised on the campaign trail with what has arrived. Watching and skeptical viewers get a careful update on a story full of smoke.
